title: De altitudine columnarum sub proprio pondere corruentium

deep.reconstruction: This page continues the logarithmic tables from p.189. Euler is summing two alternating power series, Q and Q′, in the parameter t, evaluated at the trial value t = 200; the constant 2,3010300 added each line is log10(200). The series come from his analysis of a cylindrical column buckling under its own weight. On the next page Q and Q′ are combined with the similar series P and P′ in the criterion P(1+Q′) = QP′, which decides whether t = 200 is the critical value. Each Roman-numeral term is obtained from the previous one by the recurrence log T_n = log T_{n-1} + log t − log D_n. Recomputing the subtracted logarithms shows D_n = (n+1)(3n+1)(3n+2)/n = 9(n+1)^2 + 2 + 2/n. The values are 731,25, 902,22, 1091,2, 1298,18, 1523,17 and 1766,15 for n = 8 to 13, whose logs are 2,86407, 2,95531, 3,03790, 3,11334, 3,18275 and 3,24703. The factors (n+1)/n telescope, so T_n ∝ (−t)^n / [(n+1) ∏_{k≤n}(3k+1)(3k+2)]. This is an x^{3n+1}-type series of Airy/Bessel order-1/3 type: the natural solution of θ'' + (q/EI)xθ = 0 for the heavy column. Each Q′ term is the Q term divided by (3n+1): VIII′ = VIII/25, IX′ = IX/28, …, XIII′ = XIII/40. Antilogarithms and running sums are otherwise correct. The partial sums give Q ≈ 2,7284 and Q′ ≈ 1,4980, which are carried to §37. There Euler finds P(1+Q′) = 0,4331 against QP′ = 0,4450 and concludes that t = 200 is very slightly too large.
errors: log D_12 is printed as 3,1727474. The recurrence D_12 = 13·37·38/12 = 1523,1667 gives log = 3,1827474: a single-digit slip (7 for 8) in the second decimal place.
The wrong value is actually used in the subtraction (1,1923444 − 3,1727474 = 8,0195970). So l XIII should be 8,0095970, and XIII should be about +0,0102, not +0,0105.
Through l XIV the slip propagates: l XIV should be about 7,06360, so XIV is about −0,00116 rather than −0,0012. The corrected Q is about 2,7281 instead of 2,7284.

In the Q′ column the term XIII′ (+0,0002 printed; it should be about +0,0003) is not added: the running sum stays at 1,4980 instead of 1,4982 or 1,4983. The term XIV′ (≈ −0,00003) is omitted altogether.
All these discrepancies shift the products of §37 only in the fourth decimal (QP′ ≈ 0,4450 → 0,4450; P(1+Q′) ≈ 0,4331 → 0,4332). They do not affect Euler's conclusion about t ≈ 200.

ideas.what: Evaluating alternating power series for the self-weight buckling problem term by term with base-10 logarithms, at a trial value of the load parameter. The aim is to test a transcendental criticality condition P(1+Q′) = QP′ by trial and error.
ideas.modern_name: Power-series (Frobenius / Airy–Bessel order 1/3) solution of the heavy-column eigenvalue problem; numerical root finding by trial
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1778–80 column papers); the closed Bessel-function solution is credited to Greenhill (1881)
ideas.where_published: E510 itself and the companion column papers of 1778–80 (Acta Acad. Sci. Petrop.)

ideas.what: Recurrence ratio of the series terms, D_n = (n+1)(3n+1)(3n+2)/n, and the derived series Q′ with terms divided by (3n+1).
ideas.modern_name: Coefficient recurrence of an Airy-type (Bessel J_{±1/3}) series
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (series form); Bessel/Greenhill for the identification with Bessel functions
ideas.where_published: E510, earlier sections defining the series P, Q, P′, Q′

missed.claim: There is an unnoticed computational slip in Euler's table: the divisor log for term XII→XIII is 3,1727474 where the general law (n+1)(3n+1)(3n+2)/n requires 3,1827474. This inflates XIII and XIV by about 2.3%. The Q′ running sum also fails to add XIII′. The net effect is only about 3·10^-4 in Q and Q′, and it leaves Euler's conclusion t ≈ 200 intact. I am unsure whether the Opera omnia editors flagged it.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is only relevant for an exact critical edition or for reconstructing Euler's numerical heavy-column constant against Greenhill's value.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a purely numerical table page. The only non-obvious content is the recoverable recurrence and a small arithmetic/misprint slip with negligible effect on the result.
transcription_corrections: The Q′ entry for XIII reads '+0,0002' (partially blurred); the correct value from the recurrence would be about 0,0003. The transcription's '[?]' is appropriate.
The page header ornaments are printed fleurons; the page number is ') 190 ('.
